delete.description:
Explicit user-initiated removal of an album from the cache.

This is the ONLY path that triggers `cache.delete_album` (and
therefore the FK cascade that drops `track_fingerprints` +
`track_tags` + per-album blocklists). Intended use is the "Remove
from library" affordance on Missing albums in the UI — the user
confirms that this album is gone for good, and we're free to
discard the cached computed data along with it.

Scans never reach this path; they mark albums Missing via
`cache.save_snapshot` and preserve everything.

Returns 404 when the album_id isn't in the cache (already
removed, never cached, or wrong id). Returns 200 with the
deleted album_id on success.

post.description:
Run BPM detection or ReplayGain analysis across an album's FLACs.

Streams per-file progress + final outcome. The frontend invalidates
its `tracks` query on `done` so the new BPM/RG values land in the
track list without a manual reload.

Stream an album apply as Server-Sent Events.

Solves two problems at once:
  1. Per-file progress UX — the frontend gets a `file_started` /
     `file_done` event for each FLAC so it can show a marching spinner.
  2. The "library re-scans after every apply" flicker bug — instead of
     dropping the entire library cache, we rescan ONLY the affected
     album dir and emit an `updated_album` event with the fresh row.
     The frontend updates one tile in place.

Event sequence: see `services.apply.apply_album_changes_iter`.

get.description:
Serve cover art for an album.

Default behaviour is `?size=thumb` — a pre-extracted 384px JPEG served from
`~/.musaic/thumbs/{id}.jpg`, with `Cache-Control` and ETag headers so
browsers don't re-fetch on reload. Generated on-the-fly the first time it's
requested if the scan didn't pre-build it.

`?size=full` returns the original image — the on-disk cover.jpg if present
(preferred, kernel sendfile), otherwise the largest embedded picture.

post.description:
Embed a user-supplied image as the album's cover art.

Powers the manual-upload affordance on the album sheet — used when
the user has the right artwork in hand (clipboard, file on disk,
URL paste) and Claude can't or didn't find it.

The bytes are read into memory, validated, normalized to JPEG q95,
then funneled through the same `apply_album_changes_iter` pipeline
the AI cover flow uses, so the on-disk result is identical (every
FLAC re-embedded + cover.jpg sidecar + thumb invalidation +
post-scan check rerun). Streamed as SSE so the UI can show
per-file progress.

Wipe the cached MusicBrainz anchor for an album AND blocklist
the rejected release-group.

Escape hatch for the "wrong release-group locked in" case
(typically compilations where MB matched a same-title-but-different
release). Without the blocklist, the resolver's Tier 0c
(fingerprint vote) immediately re-derives the same wrong release-
group from the cached AcoustID matches and the user is right back
where they started. Adding the rejected MBID to the per-album
blocklist (`album_blocked_mb_release_groups`) makes the rejection
sticky across all three tiers + AI persistence.

Publishes a single `AlbumTagsChanged` event so SSE consumers
invalidate their caches. The frontend's
`['album-resolution', id]` refetch re-runs the resolver on demand
via `GET /api/albums/{id}/resolution`, which is where Tier 0b/0c
will (or won't) re-derive a new anchor — and where that path
publishes `AlbumMbAnchorSet` as a side effect if it does.
Concentrating the resolver call in one place avoids the previous
double-publish + concurrent-rerun race where both the endpoint
and the resolver side-effect fired for one user action.

get.description:
Look up MusicBrainz's canonical title + artist for a duplicate
cluster's recording_mbid. Powers the resolve dialog's "MB says: …"
line, which lets the user disambiguate which mistagged file is which.

Lazy-loaded (this endpoint hits MB live, the check itself doesn't) so
the duplicate-tracks check stays fast — most clusters never have
their dialog opened. Recordings are immutable, so a single lookup
per MBID per server lifetime is sufficient (cached via
mb_lookup.get_recording_canonical's lru_cache).

  {title: null, artist: null, reason: …}  — no MBID, MB miss, or HTTP error

get.description:
Re-derive the duplicate cluster for a finding against *current*
track_fingerprints + on-disk file state.

Same architectural shape as the filename-mismatch plan-preview:
the finding's `detail.filenames` is a snapshot from check-run
time. If the user deleted a copy via another tool, re-encoded
one, or already trashed a sibling earlier, the Resolve dialog
would show ghost rows or stale tie-breaker recommendations.
This endpoint asks the check to recompute the cluster live so
the dialog always reflects right-now reality.

Response shape mirrors `Finding.detail`:
  recording_mbid, filenames, durations_s, duplicate_count,
  recommended_keep, recommended_reason. Plus:
  - `album_id`     : convenience
  - `is_empty`     : True when no duplicate cluster overlapping
                     the original finding remains — the dialog
                     should clear the stale finding
  - `removed_filenames` : entries the original finding listed but
                     that are no longer on disk / in the cluster
                     (useful for UI "X file was already trashed"
                     hints)

post.description:

Validates the filename is one of the cluster's listed duplicates (so a

the file from disk, drops the matching track_fingerprints row, and
triggers a post-scan rerun so the finding auto-resolves once the

user-confirmed rename plan. Validates the finding belongs to the

schema.title: Response Apply Filename Rename Api Checks Filename Mismatch Findings  Finding Id  Apply Post

get.description:
Re-derive the rename plan for a filename-mismatch finding against
*current* disk + settings state.

Why: the finding's `detail.renames` is a snapshot from check-run
time. If the user edits tags, manually renames files, or already
applied a sibling finding, the snapshot grows stale and the Resolve
dialog shows ghost rows that either fail to apply or re-do work
that's already done. The dialog calls this endpoint on open so it
always shows what would actually happen against the current
filesystem.

Response shape mirrors `Finding.detail` (renames, dir_rename,
template, dir_template, dir_name, headline, is_compilation) plus:
  - `album_id`     : convenience (the finding's album_id)
  - `is_empty`     : True when nothing to do — the dialog should
                      clear the stale finding and skip to next /
                      close rather than render an empty plan
  - `album_missing`: True when the album dir is gone from disk
  - `error`        : present when plan derivation crashed; in that
                      case the dialog should surface and fall back
                      to the finding's stored detail

post.description:
SSE-streamed bulk run of try_quick_fix() across every open finding
for this check. Lets the user trim the deterministic-fix portion of a
long list without committing AI work for the rest.

Pacing: one second between MB calls (MusicBrainz allows 1 req/s for
unauthenticated traffic). For 80 findings that's ~80+ seconds; we
stream per-finding outcomes so the UI can show progress.

Events emitted (event name → payload):
  - `start`    : { total }
  - `progress` : { finding_id, outcome, message }
                   outcome ∈ "fixed" | "skipped" | "error" | "not-applicable"
  - `done`     : { total, fixed, skipped, errors, not_applicable }
  - `error`    : { detail }   (only on a fatal mid-run failure)

Kick off a check. Returns the final run row when the check finishes.

For the cheap checks Phase 2 ships, runs complete in well under a second
so this is fine as a sync request. Once the heavy A1 (FLAC integrity)
check lands, we'll likely change this to fire-and-forget + SSE updates.

get.description:
Eager fingerprinting pool state — what the post-scan fpcalc /
AcoustID worker is up to. Status enum: idle | running | done |
cancelled | unavailable.

Retained for one-shot reads (status pages, tests, the rare REST
consumer). Live consumers should subscribe to
`/api/fingerprint-pool/stream` instead — the SSE channel pushes a
`state` event on every transition with no polling required.

schema.title: Response Fingerprint Pool Status Api Fingerprint Pool Status Get

get.description:
SSE stream of fingerprint-pool state transitions.

Mirrors `/api/checks/stream`: emit current state on connect, then
one `state` event per change. The pool sets a module-level
asyncio.Event after every mutation; this handler awaits with a
30-second timeout for keepalive pings.

Liveness/readiness probe. Returns as soon as the ASGI app can
serve a request — no DB, no scan state, no checks. The Electron
main process backoff-polls this until it returns 200 before
pointing the renderer at the sidecar origin.

SSE stream of `library_events` bus events.

Drives frontend cache invalidation: instead of every mutation
handler remembering a checklist of `qc.invalidateQueries` calls,
the frontend's `useLibraryEventsStream` subscribes here once and
invalidates by event name. See `docs/connectivity_design.md`.

Each event arrives as a named SSE event (event: AlbumTagsChanged,
etc.) with a JSON payload carrying the event's identity fields
(album_id, fields, source, etc.).

Per-connection bounded queue (256 events); if a client falls
behind, the oldest events are dropped with a warning and the
client is expected to refetch on the next event it sees. This is
a "something changed" signal, not durable state.
